## Configuration

Add the filter to a Typst format, and set the options under `extensions` and then `typst-extras` in the front matter.
No module runs until its option or its markup is present.

```yaml
format: typst
number-sections: true
crossref:
  chapters: true
filters:
  - typst-extras
extensions:
  typst-extras:
    list-of:
      kinds: [fig, tbl, lst]
      titles:
        lst: "Code examples"
      page-break: false
    watermark:
      text: "DRAFT"
      opacity: 15%
      angle: -45deg
      colour: gray
    sections:
      appendix-delimiter: "."
      supplementary-prefix: "S"
```

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list-of` | boolean, list or map | none | Add lists of floats at the start of the body. |
| `list-of.kinds` | `true` or list | `true` | The kinds to list. |
| `list-of.titles` | map | none | A title for one kind, which replaces the default title. |
| `list-of.page-break` | boolean | `false` | Put a page break between the lists and after the last one. |
| `watermark` | string or map | none | Draw a watermark on every page. A string is the text. |
| `watermark.text` | string | none | The text. Set `text` or `image`, not both. |
| `watermark.image` | string | none | The path of an image, relative to the document. |
| `watermark.opacity` | percentage | `15%` | The opacity of the text, from `0%` to `100%`. An image does not accept it. |
| `watermark.angle` | angle | `-45deg` for text, `0deg` for an image | The rotation, in `deg` or `rad`. |
| `watermark.size` | length | `4em` | The size of the text, in `pt`, `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `em`. |
| `watermark.colour` | colour | `gray` | The colour of the text. See [the colour values](#watermark-colour). |
| `watermark.position` | string | `center` | Where the watermark sits. |
| `watermark.width` | percentage or length | `50%` | The width of an image, as a percentage or in `pt`, `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `em`. |
| `sections.appendix-delimiter` | string | `"."` | The text between the appendix letter and the number. |
| `sections.supplementary-prefix` | string | `"S"` | The prefix of supplementary headings and floats. |

: Typst Extras options. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[27,16,17,40]"}

The extension also reads these Quarto options:

| Option | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `crossref.chapters` | Prefix floats, equations, callouts and theorems with the chapter number. |
| `number-sections` | Number the headings. Chapter prefixes need it. |
| `crossref.appendix-title` | The label of an appendix heading. The default is the language word for Appendix. |
| `crossref.appendix-delim` | The text after the appendix letter in a heading. The default is `" —"`. |
| `crossref.sec-prefix` and `crossref.ch-prefix` | The prefixes that Quarto writes in a reference to a section or a chapter. A reference to an appendix or supplementary heading with one of these prefixes shows the default label. |
| `crossref.custom` | Custom float kinds, which `list-of` accepts as kinds. |
| `lof` and `lot` | Quarto's own lists, which `list-of` must not repeat. |

: Quarto options that the extension reads. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[28,72]"}

## Lists of floats

The `list-of` option adds one list for each kind of float that has at least one float in the document.
A kind with no float adds nothing, not even a heading.

There are three forms:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-extras:
    list-of: true
```

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-extras:
    list-of: [fig, lst]
```

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-extras:
    list-of:
      kinds: [fig, lst]
      titles:
        lst: "Code examples"
      page-break: true
```

- The kinds are `fig`, `tbl`, `lst`, and every key of `crossref.custom`.
- With `true`, the order is figures, tables, listings, then the custom kinds in alphabetical order.
  With a list, the order is the order of the list.
  A kind that the list names more than once gives one list, at its first position.
- A title comes from `titles`, else from the language of the document (`crossref-lof-title`, `crossref-lot-title` and `crossref-lol-title`).
  A custom kind uses its `latex-list-of-description`, else its name.
- The lists start the body, so in Quarto's default Typst format they come after the table of contents.
  A template that places the start of the body elsewhere also moves the lists.
- Page breaks are off by default, as for `lof` and `lot`.
  With `page-break: true`, a break sits between the lists and after the last one.

::: {.callout-warning}
If `lof` or `lot` is true and `list-of` lists the same kind, the list appears twice.
The render warns.
Remove one of the two options.
:::

## Alternative text for formulas

Add an `alt` attribute to a span that holds only one formula, or to a div that holds only one display formula.
Typst writes the text into the PDF for screen readers.

```markdown
The energy is [$E = mc^2$]{alt="E equals m c squared"}.

::: {alt="The sum of the first n integers equals n times n plus one, over two."}
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \frac{n (n + 1)}{2}
$$
:::
```

- This module needs no option.
- A formula with a label (`{#eq-energy}`) is left to Quarto, which already handles `alt` on a labelled equation.
- The text can contain double quotes, backslashes and curly quotes.
  The extension escapes them for Typst.
- In other formats, the extension removes the `alt` attribute and keeps the formula.
  A span or div that has only the `alt` attribute is removed too.
  A span or div with an identifier, a class or another attribute stays, without `alt`.

## Sections

### Numbering

Numbers are flat by default, as in a Quarto article: `Figure 1` and `(1)`.
With `crossref.chapters: true` and `number-sections: true`, floats, equations, callouts and theorems get the number of the level-1 heading: `Figure 3.1` and `(3.1)`.
The numbers restart at every numbered level-1 heading.

- Without `number-sections`, the render warns and the numbers stay flat.
- The extension sets `theorem-inherited-levels` to `1` for this, so a theorem restarts at each level-1 heading.
  This replaces a value that your template sets.
- In a book, Quarto already numbers by chapter, and the extension adds nothing to that.

### Appendices

Put the class `.appendix` on a level-1 heading to start an appendix section.
The section is that heading and every block up to the next level-1 heading.
Appendix sections move to the end of the body, in source order, before the bibliography.

```markdown
# Extra results {.appendix}

Text of the appendix.

## Detail

More text.
```

| Item | Reads as |
| --- | --- |
| Level-1 heading | `Appendix A — Extra results` |
| Sub-heading | `A.1 Detail` |
| Figure, table or listing | `Figure A.1` |
| Equation | `(A.1)` |
| Reference to the section | `Appendix A` |
| Reference to the sub-heading | `Appendix A.1` |
| Reference without a prefix (`-@sec-extra`) | `A` |
| Reference with your own prefix (`[Annex @sec-extra]`) | `Annex A` |

: Appendix numbering with the default options. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

- Appendix headings are always lettered, even without `number-sections`.
  Without `number-sections`, sub-headings have no number, so you cannot refer to them.
- Floats, equations, callouts and theorems in an appendix always have the prefix.
- `sections.appendix-delimiter` sets the text between the letter and the number.
  An empty string gives `Figure A1` and `(A1)`.
- The label comes from `crossref.appendix-title`, and the separator from `crossref.appendix-delim`.
- A section moves once.
  The heading that ends it stays where it was.
- The extension scans top-level blocks only.
  A class on a heading inside a div or a callout does nothing, and does not warn.
- A class on a heading that is not at level 1 stays in place, and the render warns.
- A heading with both `.appendix` and `.supplementary` is an appendix, and the render warns.

### Supplementary sections

Put the class `.supplementary` on a level-1 heading.
These sections move to the end, after the appendices, and use the journal style.

| Item | Reads as |
| --- | --- |
| Heading | `S1 Raw data` |
| Sub-heading | `S1.1` |
| Figure or table | `Figure S1`, `Table S1` |
| Equation | `(S1)` |
| Reference to the section | `S1` |
| Reference with your own prefix (`[Table @sec-raw]`) | `Table S1` |

: Supplementary numbering with the default options. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

- Floats form one sequence across all supplementary sections.
- `sections.supplementary-prefix` sets the prefix.
- The heading has no label word, because Quarto has no language key for it.
  The heading text is the text you wrote.

### Books

In a Typst book, the book numbers the chapters and builds the appendices.

- Use the book's `appendices:` list for appendices.
  The class `.appendix` does nothing in a book, and the render warns.
- Put `.supplementary` on the level-1 heading of a chapter.
  The chapter stays in place, and its headings, floats, equations, callouts and theorems read `S1`.
- All supplementary chapters of the book share one sequence: `S1`, `S2` for the chapters, and `Figure S1`, `Figure S2` for the floats.
  This is also true when body chapters come between them.
- A body chapter after a supplementary chapter keeps the body numbering.
  For example, after chapters `1`, `2` and `S1`, the next chapter is `3`.
- The lists of floats, the alternative text and the watermark work as in a single document.

## Watermark

The `watermark` option draws text or an image on every page.
The watermark sits in the page foreground and inside an artefact, so Quarto's logo stays and screen readers skip it.

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-extras:
    watermark: "DRAFT"
```

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-extras:
    watermark:
      image: logo-faded.svg
      position: bottom-right
      width: 30%
```

- Set `text` or `image`, not both.
- An image has no `opacity`, because Typst has no such setting for images.
  Fade the image file before you use it.
  Setting `opacity` with an image is an error.
- [`colour`]{#watermark-colour} accepts a Typst colour name or a hex value, such as `"#cc0000"`.
  The names are `black`, `gray`, `silver`, `white`, `navy`, `blue`, `aqua`, `teal`, `eastern`, `purple`, `fuchsia`, `maroon`, `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `olive`, `green` and `lime`.
- `position` is one of `center`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left` and `bottom-right`.
- In a book, the watermark also shows on the cover page.

## Validation

These problems stop the render with an error that starts with `[typst-extras]`:

- `extensions.typst-extras` is not a map, or has a key that is not `list-of`, `watermark` or `sections`.
  The message names the key and lists the known keys.
- `list-of` has a value that is not `true`, a list or a map, or one of its parts has the wrong type.
- `list-of` is an empty list, or `list-of.kinds` is `false` or an empty list.
- The `list-of` map has a key that is not `kinds`, `titles` or `page-break`.
- `list-of` names a kind that is not known.
  The message lists the known kinds.
- `sections` is not a map, or has a key that is not `appendix-delimiter` or `supplementary-prefix`.
- `sections.appendix-delimiter` or `sections.supplementary-prefix` is not a string.
- `watermark` has an unknown key, sets both `text` and `image`, sets neither, or gives an empty `text` or `image` string.
- `watermark` sets `opacity` with an `image`.
- A watermark value is not valid: `opacity`, `angle`, `size`, `colour`, `position` or `width`.
  `opacity` must be from `0%` to `100%`, `size` must use `pt`, `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `em`, and `width` must be a percentage or use one of these units.

These problems let the render finish, with a warning:

- A top-level `typst-extras:` block is in the front matter.
  The extension ignores it, and the warning tells you to move it under `extensions: typst-extras:`.
- `list-of` lists a kind that `lof` or `lot` also lists.
- `crossref.chapters` is true and `number-sections` is not.
- `.appendix` or `.supplementary` is on a heading that is not at level 1.
- `.appendix` is on a chapter heading in a book.
- A heading has both `.appendix` and `.supplementary`.

## Limitations

- Every module acts on Typst output only.
  In other formats, the document stays as it is, except that the `alt` attribute on a formula is removed.
- Sub-figures lose the prefix in a reference when chapter numbers are on.
  The parent figure reads `Figure 2.2`, and `@fig-left` reads `Figure 2a`.
  Quarto builds the sub-figure number inside its own function.
  Refer to the parent figure when the number must be exact.
- With chapter numbers on, a float before the first numbered level-1 heading reads `Figure 0.1`.
  Put the first float after the first numbered level-1 heading.
- Floats in a wide block (`column: page` and similar) keep flat numbers, because Quarto gives them their own numbering.
- The numbering needs Quarto's `numbering.typ` in the template.
  A custom format that replaces the whole `template.typ` without `$numbering.typ()$` breaks the wraps.
- The table of contents and the running headers show the full label, `Appendix A — Title`.
- The watermark also shows on the cover page of a book.
- The section classes need the heading that Typst sees as level 1 to be the top heading level of the document.
  Quarto's own shift of `-1` for a document with `##` headings only works.
  A positive `shift-heading-level-by`, or a `#` heading inside a div while the top-level headings are `##`, is not supported.
- An appendix or supplementary heading that is also `.unnumbered` cannot be referenced.
- Typst counts theorems in appendix and supplementary sections with queries, so the cost grows with the number of floats.
- The tests of the extension that read PDF text need `pdftotext`, which comes with poppler.
